pr_title: Unify SendContent cancellation between HTTP3 and HTTP2
pr_body:
This PR makes sure that the `CancellationToken` used to cancel `SendContentAsync` lives is valid throughout the Task lifetime.

Fixes #60253.
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
This PR makes sure that the `CancellationTokenRegistration` used to cancel `_sendContentCts` lives throughout the `SendContentAsync` Task lifetime. Fixes #60253.
Author: rzikm
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`
Milestone: -

I think this behavior is still incorrect. We should never be disposing the CTS we hand to the user before the user is done with it.

I believe we should mirror HTTP2's cancellation logic here:
- Have a [single `_requestBodyCancellationSource` CTS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L82) that is never disposed
- This CTS is [passed to the user](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L202) when copying the request content
- This CTS is signaled (`Cancel`) on [GOAWAYs, RST_STREAMS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L885), [Dispose](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L1460) ...
- In case of duplex contents, the `CancellationToken` passed to `SendAsync` [is not used for canceling the request content](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Connection.cs#L1911)

> I think this behavior is still incorrect. We should never be disposing the CTS we hand to the user before the user is done with it.

AFAICT, the `_sendContentCts` that gets passed to `SendContentAsync` is never disposed.

> I believe we should mirror HTTP2's cancellation logic here:

I think the only thing that is missing is canceling the CTS in `Dispose` and when the stream is aborted and not cancelling with duplex content, these should be easy to fix I think.
 
> * Have a [single `_requestBodyCancellationSource` CTS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L82) that is never disposed

We have `_sendContentCts`, which is never disposed.

> * This CTS is [passed to the user](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L202) when copying the request content

We are passing the associated token (see the `sendContentCancellationToken` variable)

> * This CTS is signaled (`Cancel`) on [GOAWAYs, RST_STREAMS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L885), [Dispose](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5c57f2c0cda44176e237574ceb51d659ef9915fa/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L1460) ...

The token will be signalled on GOAWAY, via `_goawayCancellationToken` -> `_requestCancellationSource` -> `_sendContentCts` chain, stream reset and dispose are missing ATM.

Am I right, @MihaZupan, or am I missing something more?

> AFAICT, the _sendContentCts that gets passed to SendContentAsync is never disposed.

You're right, I misread this part.

> The token will be signalled on GOAWAY, via _goawayCancellationToken -> _requestCancellationSource -> _sendContentCts chain

I don't think we need dedicated CTSs for GOAWAY and Content. HTTP/2 does something more like:
- Keep `_requestBodyCancellationSource`, but initialize it in the ctor
- Remove `_goawayCancellationSource`, signal `_requestBodyCancellationSource` instead
- Register `SendAsync`'s `cancellationToken` to cancel `_requestBodyCancellationSource` during the lifetime of `SendAsync`. No need to check `IsDuplex` in this case either.
- Remove `_sendContentCts`, pass `_requestBodyCancellationSource.Token` to `SendContentAsync` instead
- Never dispose `_requestBodyCancellationSource`
@MihaZupan can you take another look please?

Should be ready for the final review, thanks all for the feedback.

issue_context.title: HTTP/3 request HttpContent cancellation is different from HTTP/2
issue_context.body:
The behavior of the `CancellationToken` passed to `HttpContent.CopyToAsync` differs between HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

Both [HTTP/2](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/9dcde5f8a182a9202a50afa92fec463f6654ecd9/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Stream.cs#L202) and [HTTP/3](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http3RequestStream.cs#L158-L165) use dedicated `CancellationTokenSource`s that are used to signal the `HttpContent` in case of a server reset / GoAway / connection-level failure / dispose.

The notable difference is that on HTTP/3, the `CancellationTokenRegistration` will be [disposed when `SendAsync` returns](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http3RequestStream.cs#L310). After that point, the CT the content is using is effectively `CT.None`.
This may delay cancellation until a write is attempted (which could take a while in duplex scenarios).

Is this the intended behavior? The choice to dispose the CTR and stop signaling the CT seems odd compared to HTTP/2.

Original YARP discussion: https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/pull/1271#discussion_r725267658

Milestone: -

Thanks for raising that up.

Do I understand it right that the problem is mostly in aborting stream on the wire and not in showing the exception to the user?

I agree that HTTP/3 seems to be missing GOAWAY cancellation logic after SendAsync completes. This should be fixed.

I also see that AbortWrite on Exception only happens [while inside SendAsync](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http3RequestStream.cs#L299-L301); meaning if any exception occurs after SendAsync finishes, AbortWrite will be postponed until Http3ResponseStream is disposed -- [WriteRequestContentAsync](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Connection.cs#L1913-L1918) doesn't have any Exception logic, while [ReadResponseContent](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http3RequestStream.cs#L1042) does. 


**For other scenarios:**

External CancellationToken passed to SendAsync does not affect streaming as soon as SendAsync completes - that is intentional and I believe HTTP/2 also behave in the same manner, so disposing HttpResponseMessage is used for cancellation. See discussion in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/30791 and
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Connection.cs#L1913-L1918

Disposing HttpResponseMessage/Http3RequestStream [properly aborts](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/565ff522bf630ff0556f3dc590dcb7337696a5d4/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http3RequestStream.cs#L88) the stream on the wire.

Also, peer aborting on the wire will be handled inside msquic; correct exception will bubble up upon attempting to write. There is a (now internal) QuicStream API to detect peer aborting right away without writing https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/58229 It was added for Kestrel but I see how it might be useful for HttpClient side too.

> Do I understand it right that the problem is mostly in aborting stream on the wire and not in showing the exception to the user?

It's more so that the HttpContent may spend a significant amount of time before reacting if the CT isn't signaled. It will still see the error, but only when attempting the next write.

> External CancellationToken passed to SendAsync does not affect streaming as soon as SendAsync completes - that is intentional and I believe HTTP/2 also behave in the same manner, so disposing HttpResponseMessage is used for cancellation.

That's correct, we do account for this in YARP logic.

@MihaZupan could you please help me understand the scenario -- where and when the exception is expected? I am only familiar with duplex streaming from gRPC perspective or a very simple custom HttpContent like [this one](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d8acd7e7ff4f54efaf170e098eb592309a610219/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/tests/FunctionalTests/HttpClientHandlerTest.Http3.cs#L1356-L1387), so maybe I miss something. If SendAsync is finished and no one is writing to the stream -- which method should throw?

@MihaZupan Is this about the cancellation token passed to your custom HttpContent's `SerializeToStreamAsync` override? And it not being ever canceled in H/3 after `SendAsync` portion of logic finishes?

So you're stuck waiting for another data to arrive from the front-end, while the back-end might have cut the connection long time ago. And instead of ending the whole session immediately (cancelling the read via the cancellation token), you need to first consume some data and then you'll learn of the connection abort (or whatever different reason) only from calling `stream.WriteAsync`.
Yes, that's a good way to describe it.
Triage: HTTP/3 should do the same thing as HTTP/2 and cancel `HttpContent` upon any exception.

review_comments:
If I get this right, the cancellation of `cancellationToken` passed into `HttpClient.SendAsync` will trigger cancellation of `_requestBodyCancellationSource` regardless of being duplex or not.

Whereas in H/2 I see that we ignore the user token for duplex contents:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/35f66ed7cb42a3fbcc2c56604c31f8a64dbe119b/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/SocketsHttpHandler/Http2Connection.cs#L1911-L1914

If the goal of this PR to have parity with H/2, I think we should take duplex into account here as well. But I might be missing something, so please correct me if I'm wrong.

> If I get this right, the cancellation of cancellationToken passed into HttpClient.SendAsync will trigger cancellation of _requestBodyCancellationSource regardless of being duplex or not.

Yes, but only before SendAsync returns (we dispose the registration).
Http2 effectively does the same thing - if the cancellation token is signaled within SendAsync, it will cancel the ReadResponseHeaders, which will in turn cancel the content.

I think this may be fine as-is, the logic is just simpler here since we're not split between 2 classes (connection & stream) and the cancellation control is therefore more explicit.
With H2 we can't pass the CT directly into SendRequestContent as the content sending may outlive the SendAsync CT. With H3, we're already using a separate CTS, so we can control the linked registration lifetime.

Yeah, H2 does it, though in a very roundabout way...
BTW we've already fixed the problem when a token was (wrongly) conditional before here https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/57619

>  it will cancel the ReadResponseHeaders, which will in turn cancel the content.

Baah, I missed that.
Seems like we want to keep the registration unconditional. so I reverted the change I proactively did about that :D

From RFC:

>    *  Upon receipt of a GOAWAY frame, if the client has already sent
      requests with a Stream ID greater than or equal to the identifier
      contained in the GOAWAY frame, those requests will not be
      processed.  Clients can safely retry unprocessed requests on a
      different HTTP connection.  A client that is unable to retry
      requests loses all requests that are in flight when the server
      closes the connection.
